scenario: AITA for no longer cooking for my roommate because he dumps condiments on everything? | Because I love cooking and (at the risk of sounding arrogant) I'm pretty good at it, I've always volunteered to be in charge of dinner when dividing up chores with roommates. I'm **not** saying my food is perfect. There are a lot of things I'm trying to improve on. But I learned to cook from two professional chefs, I don't have a lot of typical issues like under-seasoning or over-cooking food, and even when I'm living with other people that are also good at cooking I'm usually asked to prepare food 3+ nights a week. Even if I'm not incredible, I at least know what I'm doing. Since this comes up later: we have a shared food budget for staples/basic ingredients (pasta, broth, canned vegetables, flour, sugar, spices, etc). Half the time we'll split the cost of meat and fresh ingredients, half the time I pay for them myself and and accept booze, snacks (another roommate is a phenomenal baker), chores, or favors as payment. The problem is, one of my newer roommates puts condiments on everything he eats. I'm not just talking about things like hamburgers, chicken wings, mac and cheese, or anything else that normally gets condiments. I've seen him put ketchup, mayo, hot sauce, A1, or barbeque sauce on chili, steak, alfredo, fried rice, curry, pizza, red sauce, gumbo, ribs that are already covered in BBQ sauce... you get the idea. And that would be fine, I guess, but he A) does it without even trying the food first and B) completely smothers the food with them. I've tried to talk to him about this. I offered to make his favorite meals, but even stuff he says he likes prepared the way he says he likes it gets the same treatment. I've asked him to at least try the food first but he refuses. I've explained that it bothers me when I put effort into a meal and he treats it the same way he treats fast food and microwave dinners, but he said it was still being eaten so it didn't matter. I finally got frustrated and told him not to give me anything for fresh ingredients anymore because I was done cooking for him. He's been complaining to my other two roommates because his monthly expenses have gone way up (he doesn't cook at all, so he either eats out or buys prepackage meals) and saying that I'm being petty and over dramatic. My baking roommate says she agrees with my decision and the other roommate doesn't care, he just wants mealtimes to be less dramatic. AITA? I think I did plenty to meet him halfway.

message.reasoning: Okay, so I'm trying to figure out whether I'm being AITA (Accidentally Thinks It's About Them) in this situation. Let me start by understanding the scenario. I'm a roommate who loves cooking and is pretty good at it. I usually take charge of cooking dinner because I enjoy it and others seem to appreciate my efforts. However, one of my new roommates has a habit of putting condiments on everything he eats, regardless of what it is. He doesn't even try the food first; he just smothers it with sauces and stuff. I tried talking to him about this. I offered to make his favorite meals, but even when I cook something he supposedly likes, he still drenches it in condiments. I asked him to at least try the food before adding condiments, but he refused. I explained that it bothers me because I put effort into the meal, and he's treating it like fast food or microwave meals. He said it doesn't matter because he's still eating it. Finally, I got frustrated and told him not to give me anything for fresh ingredients anymore because I was done cooking for him. Now, he's complaining to my other roommates about his increased monthly expenses because he doesn't cook at all and now has to eat out or buy pre-packaged meals. He says I'm being petty and over-dramatic. My baking roommate agrees with my decision, and the other roommate doesn't care, just wanting meal times to be less dramatic. So, is this AITA? I think I did plenty to meet him halfway. I tried to accommodate his preferences, but he's not respecting the effort I put into cooking. I ended up setting boundaries, which seems reasonable to me. But maybe I'm overstepping or being too sensitive? I need to consider both sides. On one hand, I'm putting in effort to cook for everyone, and it's frustrating when someone doesn't appreciate it. On the other hand, maybe I'm expecting too much from him. He has his own preferences, and as long as he's eating, maybe it's not my place to control how he eats. But I also have to think about my own well-being. If cooking for him is causing me stress and frustration, it's important to set boundaries. It's okay to prioritize my own mental health and not let someone else's habits ruin my enjoyment of cooking for others. However, I should also reflect on whether I communicated my feelings clearly. Did I express that it's about the lack of appreciation rather than control? Maybe if I had framed it differently, he would have understood better. But I did try talking to him, so I can't be faulted for that. In the end, I think I'm not AITA because I was accommodating and tried to find a solution, but when it didn't work, I set a boundary. It's reasonable to expect some level of appreciation or consideration when you're putting effort into something for others.
